Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot, reporting pain and swelling in the right knee. The mechanism
of injury is consistent with the reported force of impact and the location of symptoms. Over the course of ten visits, care
progressed through a conservative plan including physical examination, targeted therapeutic exercise, and activity modification.
Teratment followed a typical trajectory, with visit frequency reduced as pain and range of motion improved. Examination
revealed effusion and tenderness along the joint line that support the reported injury, while ligamentous stability testing and
neurovascular assessment were within normal limits. The patient mentioned a minor strain to the same knee several years ago,
which had resolved completely without lasting limitation. A billing review identified one service recorded twice on the same
date; the provider acknowledged the second entry was a duplicate and it has been noted for correction. Patient is expected to
return to baseline function with continued home exercise.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
